question: On geometry where features resemble each other, does descriptor-based repair propose confident wrong answers?

independence.ground_truth: absolute-coordinate predicates written by hand per scenario
independence.matcher: scenario-blind; surface type, axis, area, bounding-box-relative position, radius
independence.negative_control: N1 deliberately mislabels the intended face and requires the harness to report resolved_WRONG=1. It does, so the zeros elsewhere in this round are meaningful.

baseline_behaviour.note: Across two similar pockets with the block lengthened, four identical holes with the block lengthened and one hole deleted, and a fillet whose radius changed and whose base was resized, every reference resolved to the intended face. The repair path was never reached.

scenarios.name: two similar pockets; one widened, block lengthened
four identical holes; block lengthened, one hole deleted
fillet radius changed, then base resized
negative control: ground truth deliberately wrong
hole deleted and re-created, block lengthened

h4_decisive_result.situation: The reference broke because its generator was replaced, so repair was the only route left.
h4_decisive_result.interpretation: The matcher's best answer was WRONG and scored PERFECTLY. Only an arbitrarily chosen margin threshold (0.05 against a measured 0.042) prevented a confident mis-repair. Score is not confidence; the margin is - and here the margin is too thin to carry a decision.

tests.note: The 125 failures are the pre-existing 'Material not found' environment limitation recorded in round 002, unchanged. No new failures.

caveats: Eight tracked references across six scenarios. Small, and still box-and-cylinder geometry.
Only one scenario forced an actual break, so the repair path has one data point. It is a decisive one, but it is one.
Edges and vertices remain unmeasured, as do sketch external geometry and document-level recompute.
